hook_text: In 1324 one king spent so much gold in Cairo that gold itself lost value. For years.
clip_script: His name was Mansa Musa, king of Mali, on his way to Mecca for the hajj. He crossed the Sahara with thousands of followers and camel after camel loaded with gold dust. In Cairo he gave gold to officials, to the poor, to mosques. His people bought everything in sight. Suddenly the city was flooded with gold, and when there is too much of something, it is worth less. An Egyptian writer said gold still had not recovered twelve years later. Musa spent so much he had to borrow money to get home. But he came back with scholars, books and an architect from Spain, and in Timbuktu he built a great mosque of mud, the Djinguereber. It is still standing today.
visual_style: A whiteboard caravan arriving at Cairo with sacks of gold; a market price chart for gold dropping; then a mud-brick mosque with wooden beams rising in Timbuktu.
pacing: Shock hook, fast story, a calm closing image of the mosque.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and follow Mansa Musa to Mecca.
